newsitem.title: UK: Profiles of members of UK monetary policy cttee.
newsitem.headline: Profiles of members of UK monetary policy cttee.

text.p: Following are brief profiles of the four outside members of the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee, whose appointment was announced by the Treasury on Monday.

Born October 1936. Before joining the London School of Economics (LSE) in 1985, he worked for 17 years as a monetary adviser at the Bank of England, becoming chief adviser in 1980. Now Norman Sosnow Professor of Banking and Finance at LSE. Goodhart's publications include "Money, Information and Uncertainty," "Monetary Theory and Practice," and "The Evolution of Central Banks." One son, three daughters.

Chief economist at British Airways Plc since 1993 and chairwoman of British Airways Pension Investment Management Ltd. Formerly chief economist at Royal Dutch Shell Group from 1989-93. From 1975 to 1982, she worked at World Bank in Washington and then was managing director of Logan Associates, a consulting group specialising in investment strategy and pricing. Recent publications have focussed on role of service, international direct investment and the impact of globalisation. A U.S. citizen who has lived in Britain since 1986, she is married with two children.

Born November 1937. Chief economic adviser to the Treasury since 1991. Previously group economic adviser at Barclays Bank from 1988-91 after 14 years at the London Business School. Outside appointments included Securities and Investment Board 1987-88, member of the International Stock Exchange Committee on Initial Public Offers in 1990 and Governor of London School of Economics since 1994. Married with three sons.

Born September 1949 in the Netherlands. Professor of International Marcoeconomics at Cambridge University since 1994. Formerly professor at Yale University 1985-94, London School of Economics 1982-85 and University of Bristol. Has been consultant to World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank and visiting scholar at International Monetary Fund. Was specialist adviser to House of Commons Treasury Select Committee. Author of six books on wide range on macro-economic issues. Married with two children.
